speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. How old is the child, and when did these bleeding symptoms first begin? Have you noticed any bruising or joint pain alongside the petechiae?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the child recently had a viral illness or fever, and have they received any new vaccinations or medications?
I need to determine if this is an acquired condition like ITP or a congenital bleeding disorder.
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Platelet Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the platelet count is normal, I need to rule out a coagulation factor deficiency or a vascular disorder. Does the child have a personal or family history of bleeding episodes, such as prolonged bleeding after circumcision or dental procedures?
REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin Time (PT) and Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT)

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since platelets, PT, and PTT are normal, this points strongly toward von Willebrand Disease. Do you have a family history of easy bruising or bleeding disorders, and does the child have any issues with bleeding after minor cuts or dental work?
REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since vWF tests are normal, I am now considering platelet function disorders like Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. Has the child had any bleeding after vaccinations or minor procedures, and do other family members have similar bleeding issues?
REQUEST TEST: Platelet Aggregation Studies

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal platelet count, coagulation profile, vWF tests, and platelet aggregation, I am considering a qualitative platelet defect like Scott syndrome or a vascular disorder like Ehlers-Danlos. Does the child have joint hypermobility, easy skin bruising, or tissue fragility?
REQUEST TEST: Bleeding Time

speaker: Doctor
text:
With all standard coagulation and platelet function tests normal, I am now looking at platelet adhesion defects that may not be captured by routine aggregation studies. Has the child ever had bleeding from the umbilical stump at birth, or are there any signs of macrothrombocytopenia on the blood smear? 
REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do the petechiae appear primarily on the lower extremities after prolonged standing, and does the child have any history of chronic liver disease or scurvy?
REQUEST TEST: Capillary Fragility Test (Rumpel-Leede) and Vitamin C Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal vascular and coagulation studies, I suspect a localized issue or a rare qualitative defect. Is the bleeding strictly limited to the nose and gums, or has there been any gastrointestinal or urinary bleeding? Are there any signs of trauma or foreign bodies in the nasal passages?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count and function tests, combined with normal coagulation profiles and vascular studies, rule out most common hemostatic disorders, leaving a rare platelet adhesion defect. DIAGNOSIS READY: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome
